definition: Phonetic Search Technology (PST) is a method of speech recognition.
details: An audio signal of speech is broken down into series of phonemes, which can be used to identify words. A string of six phonemes for example, “_B _IY _T _UW _B _IY,” represent the acronym “B2B”.

explainer.lead: PST is a speech-recognition method that matches speech by its sequence of phonemes rather than by words. It matters for finding spoken content when exact word forms are unreliable.

tiers.eli5: Instead of listening for whole words, the system listens for the basic sound pieces that make them up, then matches those.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers index audio as phoneme strings so queries match despite accents or unclear words. Pitfall: phoneme recognition errors propagate directly into false or missed matches.
tiers.paperLevel: An audio speech signal is decomposed into a series of phonemes whose string identifies words; e.g. the phoneme string _B _IY _T _UW _B _IY represents the acronym B2B. Accuracy is limited by phoneme recognition.

explainer.example: A search for “B2B” matches an utterance transcribed as the phoneme string _B _IY _T _UW _B _IY.
